segments.why_now: This slice is mostly string tables, log-level gating, and version reporting, so it gives Zigux a low-risk libbpf foothold with stable output semantics.
Path concatenation and bpffs-style pin-name sanitization are bounded helpers that can be validated without entering mkdir, statfs, unlink, or verifier-facing behavior.

The CPU mask parser is self-contained text processing that future perf-buffer and feature probes can share, and the landed helper now also carries the bounded chunk-reader interface plus the same automatic perf-buffer CPU-budget clamp that libbpf applies before it opens per-CPU buffers, which makes it a good first real port after the survey scaffold.

The exported attach, link, map, and program type string tables are a stable userspace-to-kernel bridge surface that extends the helper-first libbpf entry without pulling in object loading, ELF state, or syscall-backed behavior.

The proc fdinfo path construction, bounded map-info text parsing including map_extra, and token-preparation recovery classification can land as pure helpers without claiming procfs fopen or fclose behavior, pinned-map reuse side effects, token lifecycle parity, or fd ownership.

The reused-map compatibility comparison is a pure field-and-flag check that extends the existing file-path bridge packet without claiming bpffs reopen flow, fd duplication, or pinned-map side effects, and it preserves libbpf's bounded DEVMAP readonly-flag exception as an explicit helper contract.

After the fdinfo pathname, reused-map-name chooser, token-preparation planner, and text parser helpers land, the remaining file-path-and-handle bridge is still the smallest libbpf surface that crosses real bpffs path opens, token creation, pinned-object reopen flows, and fd ownership, so it should stay recorded explicitly as a deferred resource boundary instead of being blurred into the larger object-loader buckets.

The remaining cpu-mask-adjacent perf-buffer path is the smallest libbpf surface that still crosses live /sys cpu-mask file reads, cached possible-cpu counts, online CPU filtering, perf-event-array map updates, epoll registration, timeout-driven perf-buffer polling, and the interrupt-routing contract for perf-buffer delivery, so roadmap discipline says keep it explicit as a deferred boundary instead of quietly treating the landed parser helper and bounded wait-result bookkeeping helper as broader routing or timing parity.
This is still a bounded cluster, but it depends on bpf_object, bpf_map, and bpf_program model parity that the repo has not started yet.
The object-model and ELF collection surface is the first place mirror-tree sprawl becomes likely, so it should stay deferred until helper-first segments are proven.
BTF fixups, extern resolution, relocation recording, and load-time verifier interactions are the densest libbpf surface and need proven helper segments ahead of them.
